![](docs/img/notdavid.png)

Data-oriented wrappers around Blender's Python API, which read and write the attributes of mesh, curves and point cloud objects as NumPy arrays.

databpy started inside [Molecular Nodes](https://github.com/BradyAJohnston/MolecularNodes) and was split into a separate Python package for use in other projects.

## Installation
databpy supports Blender 5.1 and later, which use Python 3.13. Install it from PyPI with pip:

```bash
pip install databpy
```

::: {.callout-caution}

`bpy` (Blender as a Python module) is an optional dependency, so installing `databpy` inside Blender doesn't install a second copy of `bpy`. To use databpy outside Blender, install `bpy` as well with either of these commands:
```bash
# install with the bpy dependency
pip install "databpy[bpy]"

# install both packages
pip install databpy bpy
```
:::

## Usage

databpy creates objects, and stores and retrieves their attributes. [`store_named_attribute()`](https://bradyajohnston.github.io/databpy/api/store_named_attribute.html) and [`named_attribute()`](https://bradyajohnston.github.io/databpy/api/named_attribute.html) are named after the `Store Named Attribute` and `Named Attribute` nodes in Geometry Nodes, and work on mesh, curves and point cloud objects.

To store an attribute on a new object:
```python
import numpy as np
import databpy as db

coords = np.array([[0, 0, 0], [0, 5, 0], [5, 0, 0], [5, 5, 0]])

obj = db.create_object(coords, name="Box")
db.store_named_attribute(obj, np.array([10, 20, 31, 42]), "vals")
```
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2af6046a-8d73-4881-af63-8ed175fe2136)

Attributes are stored and retrieved as NumPy arrays:

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: false
import bpy
bpy.ops.wm.read_homefile(app_template="")
```


```{python}
import numpy as np
import databpy as db

np.random.seed(6)

# Create a mesh object
random_verts = np.random.rand(10, 3)

obj = db.create_object(random_verts, name="RandomMesh")

obj.name
```

Read an attribute from the object's mesh:
```{python}
db.named_attribute(obj, "position")
```


### `BlenderObject` class (bob)

`BlenderObject` wraps a `bpy.types.Object` and provides databpy's functions as methods. Wrap an existing object, or create a new one with `create_bob()`.

Attributes can be read with `named_attribute()`, or as properties and items such as `bob.position` and `bob["position"]`.

```{python}
# wrap an existing object or create a new one
bob = db.BlenderObject(obj)
bob = db.create_bob(random_verts)

# these two are identical
bob.named_attribute("position")
bob.position
```

`new_from_pydata()` clears the geometry of the object's mesh and fills it with new vertices, edges and faces:

```{python}
bob.new_from_pydata(np.random.randn(5, 3))
bob.position
```

## Example with Polars data

```{python}
import polars as pl
import databpy as db
from io import StringIO

json_file = StringIO("""
{
  "Dino": [
    [55.3846, 97.1795, 0.0],
    [51.5385, 96.0256, 0.0]
  ],
  "Star": [
    [58.2136, 91.8819, 0.0],
    [58.1961, 92.215, 0.0]
  ]
}
""")

df = pl.read_json(json_file)
columns_to_explode = [col for col in df.columns if df[col].dtype == pl.List(pl.List)]
df = df.explode(columns_to_explode, empty_as_null=True)

vertices = np.zeros((len(df), 3), dtype=np.float32)
bob = db.create_bob(vertices, name="DinoStar")

for col in df.columns:
    data = np.vstack(df.get_column(col).to_numpy())
    bob.store_named_attribute(data, col)

bob.named_attribute("Dino")
```


```{python}
bob.named_attribute("Star")
```
